title: Remote access VPN with Secure Client
blurb: Give remote employees an SSL VPN on the ASA with an address pool, split tunneling and a connection profile.
scenario: Employees working from home need to reach the inside network **10.1.1.0/24** through the ASA's **outside** interface, using **Cisco Secure Client** (formerly AnyConnect). Clients get addresses from **10.50.50.1–10.50.50.100**, use the internal DNS server **10.1.1.53**, and send only corporate traffic through the tunnel. The Secure Client package is already on the flash as **disk0:/cisco-secure-client-win-5.1.2.42-webdeploy-k9.pkg**.
topology:
Home PC ── Internet ── outside [ASA] inside ── 10.1.1.0/24 (DNS 10.1.1.53)
                            pool 10.50.50.1-100
objectives: Create the address pool and split-tunnel ACL
Turn on SSL VPN on the outside interface

steps.title: Pool and split-tunnel list
steps.learn: Each VPN client gets an inside address from a **local pool**. With **split tunneling**, only the networks in a standard ACL go through the tunnel, and other traffic goes straight to the Internet. That saves bandwidth but leaves that traffic outside the firewall's inspection.
steps.task: Create pool **VPN-POOL** from **10.50.50.1** to **10.50.50.100**, mask **255.255.255.0**. Create standard ACL **SPLIT-ACL** that permits **10.1.1.0 255.255.255.0**.
steps.hint: `ip local pool VPN-POOL 10.50.50.1-10.50.50.100 mask 255.255.255.0` and `access-list SPLIT-ACL standard permit 10.1.1.0 255.255.255.0`.

commands.note: ASA ACLs use subnet masks, not wildcard masks.

steps.title: Turn on SSL VPN
steps.learn: The `webvpn` mode turns on the SSL VPN service on an interface, names the client package that users download, and turns on the client.
steps.task: In **webvpn** mode, enable it on **outside**, load the package **disk0:/cisco-secure-client-win-5.1.2.42-webdeploy-k9.pkg** as image **1**, turn on the client, and turn on the tunnel group list.
steps.hint: `webvpn`, `enable outside`, `anyconnect image disk0:/cisco-secure-client-win-5.1.2.42-webdeploy-k9.pkg 1`, `anyconnect enable`, `tunnel-group-list enable`. The keyword is still `anyconnect` even for Secure Client.

commands.note: Users can pick their connection profile from a list at login.

steps.title: Group policy
steps.learn: A **group policy** holds the settings pushed to the client: allowed protocols, DNS, and the split-tunnel policy. You create it, then edit its attributes.
steps.task: Create internal group policy **GP-RA**. In its attributes, allow the protocol **ssl-client**, set split tunneling to **tunnelspecified** with network list **SPLIT-ACL**, and set DNS server **10.1.1.53**.
steps.hint: `group-policy GP-RA internal`, `group-policy GP-RA attributes`, `vpn-tunnel-protocol ssl-client`, `split-tunnel-policy tunnelspecified`, `split-tunnel-network-list value SPLIT-ACL`, `dns-server value 10.1.1.53`.

steps.title: Connection profile
steps.learn: The **tunnel group** (connection profile in ASDM) is what users connect to. Its general attributes set the address pool and default group policy. Its webvpn attributes set the name shown in the client's list.
steps.task: Create remote-access tunnel group **RA-VPN**. In general attributes, use pool **VPN-POOL** and default group policy **GP-RA**. In webvpn attributes, add group alias **Employees** and enable it.
steps.hint: `tunnel-group RA-VPN type remote-access`, `tunnel-group RA-VPN general-attributes`, `address-pool VPN-POOL`, `default-group-policy GP-RA`, `tunnel-group RA-VPN webvpn-attributes`, `group-alias Employees enable`.

steps.title: Split tunnel trade-off
steps.question: With this split-tunnel setup, a user at home browses a public news site. Which path does that traffic take?

options.text: Straight out of the user's home Internet connection, outside the tunnel, because only 10.1.1.0/24 is in SPLIT-ACL.
Through the tunnel to the ASA and out to the Internet from there.
options.why: That's full tunneling (tunnelall). Here, only the networks in SPLIT-ACL are tunneled.

options.text: It's blocked, because it isn't in the ACL.
options.why: The split-tunnel ACL chooses what is tunneled. It doesn't block anything.

steps.task: Show the connected Secure Client sessions.

summary: An address pool and split-tunnel ACL, SSL VPN turned on outside with the Secure Client package, a group policy with split tunneling and DNS, and the RA-VPN connection profile, verified in the VPN session database.
